public_rationale: Marcus forecast that hallucination problems will 'eventually' be ironed out. He gave no deadline. Under the contract, the forecast can be scored as supported early only if independent evidence shows hallucinations in leading chatbots are no longer a significant reliability problem across representative uses. The packet has no such evidence. Vectara's leaderboard, released in November 2025, measured hallucination rates above 10% for several leading models, including GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5. The lowest rate it reported was 3.3% (e1). In September 2025, OpenAI said GPT-5 has fewer hallucinations but 'they still occur', and that hallucinations remain 'a fundamental challenge for all large language models' (e2). Because the forecast has no deadline, the contract sets no way for it to be contradicted.
limitations: 'Ironed out' has no stated threshold, so any future judgement would need to set one.
Benchmark hallucination rates depend on the task and the dataset used.
The packet's evidence runs only to November 2025 and covers one benchmark and one developer statement.
